knowledge:
- key_parameters: numBases=number of flanking bases to consider including the central base (e.g., 5) ;; trDir=logical indicating whether to include transcription direction ;; numSig=number of mutation signatures to estimate ;; localTest=logical indicating whether to perform a local test (TRUE) or global test (FALSE) ;; refGroup=integer vector specifying the indices of the reference group samples ;; nIter=number of MCMC iterations ;; useInits=an object containing initial values (e.g., from pmgetSignature) to accelerate MCMC convergence ;; sigOrder=numeric vector specifying the plotting order of signatures
- alternatives: pmsignature is used for standard signature estimation via the EM algorithm (pmgetSignature) and visualization (pmBarplot), but HiLDA should be preferred when statistical testing of signature burden differences between two groups is required.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have somatic mutation position data from two distinct groups of samples and want to test for statistically significant differences in their mutational signature exposures.
- pitfalls: Requires external installation of JAGS (Just Another Gibbs Sampler). If the potential scale reduction statistic (Rhat) returned by hildaRhat is greater than 1.10, the MCMC chains have not converged, and nIter should be increased. Some mutations may be discarded during file reading if transcription direction information is missing.

workflows.name: mutational_signature_burden_testing
workflows.intent: Read mutation position data, perform global and local Bayesian tests to compare signature burdens between two groups, assess MCMC convergence, and visualize the signatures and exposure differences.
input: inputFile (a tab-separated text file in Mutation Position Format containing sample name, chromosome, coordinate, reference base, and alternate base)
workflows.stages: 1. Read mutation position data using hildaReadMPFile ;; 2. Estimate initial signature parameters using pmgetSignature ;; 3. Perform global and local Bayesian tests using hildaTest ;; 4. Assess MCMC convergence using hildaRhat ;; 5. Visualize signatures and exposure proportions using pmBarplot, hildaBarplot, and hildaDiffPlot
workflows.code:
library(HiLDA)
inputFile <- system.file("extdata/esophageal.mp.txt.gz", package="HiLDA")
G <- hildaReadMPFile(inputFile, numBases=5, trDir=TRUE)
load(system.file("extdata/sample.rdata", package = "HiLDA"))
set.seed(123)
hildaGlobal <- hildaTest(inputG=G, numSig=3, localTest=FALSE, refGroup=1:4, nIter=1000)
hildaLocal <- hildaTest(inputG=G, numSig=3, localTest=TRUE, refGroup=1:4, nIter=1000)
Param <- pmgetSignature(G, K = 3)
set.seed(123)
hildaGlobal <- hildaTest(inputG=G, numSig=3, useInits = Param, localTest=TRUE, refGroup=1:4, nIter=1000)
hildaLocal <- hildaTest(inputG=G, numSig=3, useInits = Param, localTest=TRUE, refGroup=1:4, nIter=1000)
hildaRhat(hildaGlobal)
hildaRhat(hildaLocal)
pmPlots <- pmBarplot(G, Param, refGroup=1:4, sigOrder=c(1,3,2))
cowplot::plot_grid(pmPlots$sigPlot, pmPlots$propPlot, rel_widths = c(1,3))
hildaPlots <- hildaBarplot(G, hildaLocal, refGroup=1:4, sigOrder=c(1,3,2))
cowplot::plot_grid(pmPlots$sigPlot, pmPlots$propPlot, rel_widths = c(1,3))
hildaDiffPlots <- hildaDiffPlot(G, hildaLocal, sigOrder=c(1,3,2))
cowplot::plot_grid(hildaDiffPlots$sigPlot, hildaDiffPlots$diffPlot, rel_widths = c(1,3))
